title: A cool fortnight: cocoons wait
about: Compost worms lay most cocoons at 20-25 °C and hardly any below 10 °C, and a cocoon needs warmth to hatch: about three weeks at 22 °C, months in the cold. Here two weeks without frost but some 9 °C colder than usual: few or no cocoons hatch, and they pile up. When it warms up the oldest hatch within about ten days.

steps.title: The helper feeds, and the air cools
steps.why: Two weeks some 9 °C colder than usual, at five hours a second. The box follows the air down to about 9 °C in its core.

steps.title: A cool fortnight
steps.why: Watch the cocoons: they wait. Only the oldest, nearly ready ones may still hatch on a mild afternoon. The worms are alive but neither breed nor grow much. The step is complete on a cool night late in the fortnight.

expect.say: hatched in the cool fortnight (simulation only): {v}

steps.title: Warm again
steps.why: The cool spell is over. Cocoons gather warmth again; the oldest hatch first, about ten days on.

steps.title: Back to normal
steps.why: The helper stops and the clock runs at its usual pace.
